findings.finding: Asked to look for other decision-carrying members the checker still skips: a one-leaf-at-a-time sweep of c6's records through check_set accepted 208 of 408 custody, 221 of 411 launcher and 491 of 1053 recipe mutations. Most are prose, paths or placeholders, but each of these single-value mutations, probed through explain(check_set) on in-memory copies, is accepted although it contradicts a decision or binding rule: (a) B-LHA-7, 'If one server identity serves both proxy kinds, the record says so': the model refuses only flagged entries that name two identities or a non-proxy kind, so the KUBERNETES_API_PROXY and CAMPAIGN_PROXY entries keeping their shared identity with servesBothProxyKinds false (one or both) are accepted, although the refusal text states the rule (unchanged since c4); (b) T1's or T2's offHost false (runbook steps 10 and 12: 'T1, off host', 'T2, off host'); (c) liveManifestInT2 set to SIGNED_IN_T2 (runbook step 12: until CONF-LIVE-005/006 close, T2 signs no live manifest); (d) nonce.hostLedger durable false, or its owner OPERATOR_UID (Q-LHA-3 (a): a root-owned durable host ledger); (e) the new localEndpointIdentities.ifTheCampaignReleaseChoosesTheLocalCa set to NOT_A_CUSTODY_SCOPE_CHANGE (MON-LHA-CR1-KEEP's OPEN-1 ruling), and host-authority.json's new G10-LOCAL-ENDPOINT-IDENTITIES with before RUNBOOK_STEP_10 or any other what: the step-7 ordering is checked in custody-model.json but not in the precondition entry; (f) access.acceptedLimit.words, the owner's Q-LHA5-1 words, replaced by any text, in the member c5 rewrote for LHA-C1-3; (g) OWNER_ADMIN's access.identities row with osLogin true (B-LHA-18); (h) access.revocation.endsAdminSessionsOn reduced to one host (B-LHA-10: every admin session on both hosts); (i) egress.paidFirewallFeature true (Q-LHA-11 (a): no paid firewall feature); (j) source.repositoryCredentialOnHost true (design revision 7 line 97, runbook step 4: no repository credential on the host); (k) the IAP_TUNNEL lease binding revoked at step 17, after the step-16 teardown, or access.teardown.keeps cut to one item; (l) offlineLauncher.manifestServesANormalInvocation true, or timeLimits.operatorMdOneHourAge relabelled (B-LHA-11's third bullet); (m) offlineLauncher.custodyBinds without POLICY_DIGEST (runbook step 10: custody.json binding the policy digest); (n) the export unit's hosts cut to the proxy/operator host while the node carries EXPORT_UNIT (B-LHA-1: each root-only record's read path at step 15). Self-contradictions with checked members pass too: principal.count 2 beside the checked single-principal disclosure (Q-LHA-1); the cluster node's holdsKubernetesClientCredential true (B-LHA-2); liveLauncher.designOnly false (design section 6). The records as published are right; the checker, which the README presents as the records' checker, accepts records that are not. MINOR, as round 1 rated this class (LHA-C1-2).

findings.location: scripts/linux_host_authority.py check_custody (perRunCredentials, tokenSessions, endpointServerIdentities), check_launcher (triggerUnits, exportSet) and _check_access (access.identities): each list indexed by a dict keyed by id
findings.finding: Each of these lists is read through a dict keyed by id, and the check compares the dict's keys, not the list's ids, with the expected ids. A repeated id keeps its first position and its last value, so a wrong entry followed by a correct copy with the same id passes, and the wrong entry is never checked. Probed through explain(check_set) on in-memory copies, each of these is accepted: perRunCredentials with its first entry reused across runs, or issued by the per-run cluster CA at STEP_8, and its correct copy appended (B-LHA-2; 'a per-run credential is never reused across runs'); tokenSessions with T1 at step 13 in reverse order and the correct T1 appended, which evades c5's T1/T2 check and the refusal text 'two token sessions per run'; endpointServerIdentities with an unlisted owner (B-LHA-7); triggerUnits with a third unit, a preflight unit run as root with another command (B-LHA-1: one unit for the preflight and one for the export, each running one fixed command; the refusal text 'one reviewed family of trigger units'); access.identities with OWNER_LOGIN administering IAM; exportSet with a host exporting nothing. No schema bound (maxItems or uniqueItems) refuses them. The indexing is unchanged since c4, and c5's new token-session and local-CA leaf checks rely on it. authorities, fixedTargets and, since c5, profile compare the id list itself and refuse a repeat.
findings.requiredChange: Compare each list's ids, in order, with the expected ids before building the dict (as check_launcher does for fixedTargets and c5 now does for profile), or refuse a repeated id by a named rule; add a refusal vector for at least one such list in each record.
